# `monaco-vim`'s CodeMirror adapter, vendored

`cm_adapter.ts` answers the CM5 editor interface (`../codemirror-vim/types.ts`'s
`CM5EditorInterface`) over a Monaco editor. It is here because it is the **reference
implementation of the members a terminal answers with the identity** — `charCoords`,
`coordsChar`, `getScrollInfo`, `scrollTo`, `defaultTextHeight`, `findPosV`, `scanForBracket` —
which in a GUI are real pixel questions, already answered against real pixels.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| origin | `https://github.com/brijeshb42/monaco-vim`, `src/cm_adapter.ts` |
| revision | `monaco-vim@0.4.4` on npm, tarball SHA-256 `a63e8d8582d8df33a49b8071a8dbf0b80c817518` (shasum), published ≈2026-04 |
| licence | MIT, `LICENSE` beside this file; `LICENSE.codemirror.txt` covers the CodeMirror lineage the file carries |

Only `cm_adapter.ts` is taken. The package's other sources are not:

| not vendored | why |
| --- | --- |
| `src/cm/keymap_vim.ts` | monaco-vim's own fork of the CM5 vim engine. This port uses replit's engine instead — one engine for the whole tree. Taking both would be two engines that drift, which is the fallback this port did not need |
| `src/index.ts` | glue binding the adapter to *that* engine, plus a status-bar wiring. `contrib/vim/tauri/` is this port's equivalent |
| `src/statusbar.ts` | a DOM status bar of its own. The mode line here is an `IStatusbarService` entry, and the `:`/`/` prompt is rendered rather than focused, so keys keep reaching the editor |

## The `main`-side patch

Two import lines, and nothing else:

```
"monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/editor.api"                        → "../../vs/editor/editor.api.js"
"monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/common/commands/shiftCommand"      → "../../vs/editor/common/commands/shiftCommand.js"
```

This port builds Monaco from source, so the API surface is present at those paths.

## What the adapter does not answer, and where that is fixed

The adapter was co-developed with monaco-vim's own engine, not with replit's, so its surface is
a **subset** of what `CM5EditorInterface` declares — measured 50 of 82 instance members and 13 of
17 statics. `contrib/vim/tauri/vimAdapter.ts` subclasses it and supplies the rest, so that this
directory stays pristine but for the two lines above. That file's header lists every member and
what each one costs while it is missing.

The one behavioural gap the splice probe found: monaco-vim ships `operation(fn) { return fn(); }`
— a stub — and compensates with four `cm.pushUndoStop()` calls patched into its own engine.
Replit's engine has none of them, so undo granularity comes from `operation`, where CM5 puts it.
The subclass implements it.

## Do not edit this file

`vendor` holds it pristine. Everything this port needs it to do differently belongs in the
subclass; `git diff vendor..main -- src/vendor` must show the two import lines and nothing else.
